extractedRows.sourceTitle: Pituitary incidentaloma: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Can support that pituitary incidentaloma evaluation includes history/physical examination, laboratory screening for hormone hypersecretion and hypopituitarism, visual field examination when near optic structures, and clinical assessment/imaging follow-up when not surgically removed.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include pituitary hormone-axis status, hypersecretion, hypopituitarism, mass effect, visual-field risk, imaging follow-up and surgical referral criteria.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Patients with pituitary incidentalomas discovered on imaging, across endocrine, ophthalmologic, neurosurgical and follow-up settings.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Pituitary lesion monitoring protects continuity through vision preservation, hormonal crisis prevention and timely treatment of mass-effect or endocrine dysfunction.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline is incidentaloma-specific; functioning tumors and known pituitary disorders may require separate disease-specific sources.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Do not use for all pituitary tumors, individual surgery decisions or calibrated visual/hormonal outcome prediction.
